stories.title: ANC faces anger over poor services as South Africans vote in local elections
bullet_points: Party expected to get less than a third of the vote amid frustration over water outages and power cuts  The African National Congress is on course for a bruising result in South Africa’s local elections on Wednesday as voters go to the polls amid deep discontent over water outages, power cuts and crumbling infrastructure.
The former liberation movement, which Nelson Mandela led to power in 1994 at the end of apartheid as South Africa’s first black president, is still likely to be the largest party.
However, polls showed it getting less than a third of the vote, down from 45.6% at the  last municipal elections  in 2021 and 40.2% in  2024’s national elections .

stories.title: Pope’s visit to Argentina sets up showdown with ‘hyper-capitalist’ Milei
bullet_points: Excitement is in the air, because on Monday 9 November, the Cottolengo Don Orione – a Catholic-run home for disabled people – will be the first stop on Pope Leo XIV’s first full day of his trip to Argentina.
But the pope’s visit to Claypole, about 26km from Buenos Aires, does not come at an especially happy time for the home, which counts about 400 residents with disabilities.
Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has made wide-ranging cuts to disability funding.

stories.title: Banana producers in Latin America want better pay to cope with effects of climate crisis
bullet_points: Farmers face big drop in production from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event  Banana producers in Latin America are calling for better pay to help cope with the impact of the climate crisis, as they face big drops in production resulting from extreme weather during this year’s super El Niño event.

High winds in parts of Colombia, one of the biggest suppliers to the UK market where droughts are predicted in some regions this year, and heavy rainfall in Peru and Ecuador are already affecting production, according to the Fairtrade Foundation ethical trade body.
In the Dominican Republic, farmers are expected to face drought conditions, with forecasts of drier and warmer than usual conditions.
